title.narrative: Water Resources Development Investment Program - Project 1

description.narrative:
The Investment Program is consistent with the Afghanistan National Development Strategy (ANDS), which was approved in April 2009 and constitutes the country's strategic platform for development for 2008-2020. Its aim is to promote growth, generate wealth, and reduce poverty and vulnerability. ANDS covers all key sectors and sub-sectors, and embraces several themes. Water resources is a major sector under ANDS, which provides a programmatic approach to developing the water sector that includes (i) physical investments in rehabilitation of existing and development of new water resources and irrigation infrastructure; and (ii) nonphysical investment in capacity building, strengthened institutions, and policy frameworks. The proposed MFF finances the medium-term portion of a broader investment program. The Investment Program is consistent with ADB's Afghanistan country partnership strategy (CPS) 2009-2013, long-term strategic framework 2008-2020 (Strategy 2020), and water policy Water for All.
The Investment Program will finance (i) the rehabilitation and upgrading of existing and development of new irrigation and water resources infrastructure, (ii) flood management infrastructure, (iii) institutional strengthening, and (iv) capacity building for key staff throughout the sector. The first tranche project has four components: (i) northern basins development (NBD) that includes rehabilitation and upgrading of irrigation infrastructure, and development of a river basin agency (RBA) and water users associations (WUAs) for water management; (ii) Nangarhar Valley Development Authority (NVDA) improvement that includes irrigation rehabilitation and upgrading, development of WUAs, and a management reform plan for the NVDA; (iii) flood management that includes development of flood protection infrastructure along the Amu Darya River and development of a national flood management program; and (iv) project management and program development that includes a program development facility to prepare the subsequent two tranches of the MFF.

description.narrative: Improved water resources management.

At least 5,000 ha and Yangi Qala town have significantly reduced flood risk by 2017. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: After completion of Yatim Tepa Flood Protection Embankment and Intake rehabilitation in Dec 2017, the districts/towns of Yangi Qala and Khaoja Bahaudin, and an equivalent of 12,000 ha of land have been protected from flood and erosion. In addition, these districts are now supplied with reliable irrigation water. Data Source: MEW quarterly reports.

Rehabilitation and upgrading irrigation systems serving at least 70,000 ha by 2017. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: So far, irrigation systems serving more than 85,000 ha have been rehabilitated and it is anticipated that more land will be reclaimed by end of 2020. As per the government's request in June 2018 additional activities were included in the procurement plan. T1 was extended until 31 December 2021. Procurement of the additional activities has been completed along with works done. The winding-up period was extended until 31 December 2023 on exceptional basis on 28 November 2022. Data Source: MEW and MAIL quarterly reports.

WUAs and Northern Basin RBA sustainably managing irrigation according to the National Water Law by 2017. Achievement: Y Progress/Status: So far, more than 10 water user associations have been established under the grant, and capacity building training in various aspects for the said associations and river basin agencies was provided by an NGO in 2018. Further, the flood management unit (FMU) is established under WRD of NWARA and various capacity-building training was supposed to be provided to the FMU personnel in Q2-Q3 2021, along with equipment support during the deposed government, therefore, this activity of the project is likely not to be achieved as the project closed by 31 December 2021, while it is unlikely ADB's operation will resume. The winding-up period was extended until 31 December 2023 on exceptional basis on 28 November 2022. Data Source: MEW RBA and NVDA quarterly and annual reports Base year: 2010 Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Improved northern Basin irrigation system delivers reliable irrigation supplies. Indicator: At least 150 improved water access points in the lower Balkh Basin and NVDA irrigation system are operational by 2016. Achievement: 280 Progress/Status: More than 280 improved water access points for women have been constructed under the NVDA contract in Nangarhar province and in the Lower Balkh by an NGO. Data Source: WUA annual reports.

Output: Improved northern Basin irrigation system delivers reliable irrigation supplies. Indicator: New Bangala Weir is operational by 2016. Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: The contract for Bangala weir construction was awarded on 21 April 2014. The works were completed in Nov 2016 and handed over to the Balkh river basin agency. The weir is currently functional. Data Source: MEW annual reports.

Output: Improved northern Basin irrigation system delivers reliable irrigation supplies. Indicator: The NVDA irrigation system provides water with design discharge in 100% of the command areas in Nangarhar province by 2016. Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: The invitation for bids for procurement of works for rehabilitation of Nangarhar Valley Development Authority (NVDA) main, secondary and tertiary canals was advertised on 21 Aug 2013 and the contract was awarded on Feb 3, 2015. Physical works of NVDA were completed on 13 June 2017 and the system is now operational.
In addition, two newly added civil works contracts through national competitive bidding have been awarded and works are completed. These packages have improved the efficiency at the NVDA irrigation system.
Data Source: WUA annual reports.

Output: Capacity development and training Indicator: Irrigation service delivery and O&M plan for NVDA irrigation system adopted by NVDA by December 2017. Achievement: y Progress/Status: Irrigation service delivery and the establishment of irrigation associations (IA) was part of SNC-Lavalin's, the consulting firm, contract under the grant which withdrew from the country in 2014. In 2017 an NGO was recruited by MAIL to establish IAs in Nangarhar and Balkh provinces and provide the required capacity building training to the IAs.
O&M for NVDA was prepared in 2017 by Sim S.P.A, the supervision consulting team under the project, and has been adopted. Data Source: MAIL quarterly and annual reports. Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: n Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: n Target year: 2017 Target value: Y Actual value: y

Output: Capacity development and training Indicator: NVDA institutional reform and business plan submitted to MAIL by 2017. Achievement: y Progress/Status: Progress on this component was slow due to the involvement of a number of government agencies and line departments. However, the charter was developed in January 2013 and approved by the Minister's council (MoC) in September 2014. An International Business Plan Specialist was recruited in October 2017 who developed a business plan for NVDA. The business plan was approved by the President in Q1 2018 and being implemented. Data Source: MAIL quarterly and annual reports. Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: n Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: n Target year: 2017 Target value: Y Actual value: y

Output: Capacity development and training Indicator: National Flood Management Unit within MEW operating by December 2017. Achievement: N Progress/Status: The concept paper for the establishment of the Flood Management Unit (FMU) was prepared by SNC Lavalin, an international consulting firm, in 2014 and was approved by the National Water Affairs Regulatory Authority (NWARA) (previously known as MEW). The FM unit under WRD of NWARA was operating and project support was supposed to be extended within 2021 under the previous government, for which procurement was ongoing and expected to be completed by end Q3 2021. However, due to the previous government deposed in mid-August 2021, ADB placed hold on its assistance in Afghanistan, effective 15 August 2021. Data Source: MEW/MAIL quarterly and annual reports. Output: Improved northern Basin irrigation system delivers reliable irrigation supplies. Indicator: 250 upgraded secondary canal irrigation structures pass their design discharge safely by 2014. Achievement: y Progress/Status: 207 upgraded secondary canal irrigation structures were completed and handed over on 31 October 2014. All the structures are currently functional. Due to some unforeseen reasons i.e. community concerns where the structures were located and changes in the design of the structures the contractor was not able to complete construction of all 250 structures. Such changes in design increased volume of the works which increased the cost of the contract by 15%. A change in the scope of the contract was approved by ADB in 2014.
Data Source: Provincial Government irrigation data MEW irrigation system operation data. Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2010 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y Actual value: y

Output: Irrigated lands are protected from flood events Indicator: 5 km of bank protection along river bank at diversion structures in Takhar province operating by 2017. Achievement: y Progress/Status: Invitation for bids for Yatim Tepa flood protection works and pilot porcupines contract was advertised on 22 October 2013. ADB's no-objection was granted for award of the contract on 3 September 2014 and the contract was signed on 21 October 2014. The Notice To Proceed was issued on 17 January 2015 by MEW. The head regulator for Yatim Tepa intake was completed in December 2017 and it is fully functional. 5.6 Km flood embankment along the Amu River in Yangi Qala town has been completed and it is currently operational.
